channel.title: Threat Desk
channel.description: Vulnerabilities, advisories and threat activity, twice a day

item.title: Samsung Securities breach exposes 8,241 customer records
item.description: Personal data including names, addresses, and account numbers for thousands of Samsung Securities customers has been exposed online following a reported data breach.

item.title: Bluetooth flaws in Elecbrakes controllers allow remote brake manipulation
item.description: Researchers demonstrated that unauthenticated attackers within 100 metres can engage or release trailer brakes, posing a severe physical safety risk.

item.title: UK NCSC reports marked rise in AI-assisted cyberattacks
item.description: Britain's National Cyber Security Centre warns that AI agents are accelerating attacks on existing weaknesses, urging organisations to reinforce basic security controls.

item.title: Two unrelated database leaks expose 3.5 billion credentials
item.description: Researchers found two separate databases containing billions of usernames, passwords, and identity documents left exposed to the public internet.

item.title: Gleneagles Hospital HK suspends app after data breach
item.description: Gleneagles Hospital Hong Kong has suspended its patient mobile application following the detection of unauthorised access to sensitive personal data.

item.title: Carnegie Endowment donor data leaked via Soapbox Engage breach
item.description: A cyberattack on third-party fundraising platform Soapbox Engage exposed donor contact details and giving history for the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace.

item.title: Radware breach exposes customer cloud log export credentials
item.description: An unauthenticated internal API exposed customer contact details and cloud storage keys, prompting Radware to advise immediate credential rotation.

item.title: Turnitin detects unauthorized activity in customer-facing systems
item.description: Educational technology firm Turnitin has disclosed a cyberattack affecting its customer-facing systems, with no confirmation yet of data theft or service disruption.

item.title: McDonald's Japan breach exposes app user location and purchase data
item.description: McDonald's Japan confirmed a database breach affecting its official mobile app, exposing customer location data and purchase histories without revealing the scale of the incident.

item.title: European Commission confirms data theft in EU Academy breach
item.description: The European Commission confirmed that an AI-assisted cyberattack resulted in the compromise of user names and email addresses on its EU Academy platform.

item.title: Colorado shuts down myColorado app after data breach
item.description: The state's digital ID and services app is offline after an unauthorised breach that may have exposed data for up to 150,000 users.

item.title: Broadcom patches critical VMware ESX and vCenter flaws
item.description: Broadcom has released cumulative updates for 23 vulnerabilities, including critical authentication bypass and code execution issues in VMware ESX and vCenter.

item.title: Drupal core RCE flaw exploited in the wild
item.description: CISA and Drupal confirm active exploitation of CVE-2026-132165, a remote code execution vulnerability in the core installer patched on 18 November.

item.title: Palo Alto patches Fragnesia flaw exploited to root firewalls
item.description: Palo Alto Networks has released PAN-OS updates to address CVE-2026-46300, a Linux kernel vulnerability exploited in conjunction with PHP2Shell to gain root access on internet-exposed firewalls.

item.title: CISA adds three actively exploited vulnerabilities to KEV Catalog
item.description: CISA has listed three new vulnerabilities in its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog, citing evidence of active exploitation that poses significant risks to the federal enterprise.

item.title: CISA warns of heap overflow in AutomationDirect C-More EA9 software
item.description: A heap-based buffer overflow in C-More EA9 Programming Software could allow arbitrary code execution if users open a malicious file.

item.title: Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA controller vulnerable to unauthenticated stack-based buffer overflow
item.description: CISA has issued an advisory for a critical stack-based buffer overflow in Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA Series controllers that hypothetically allows potential arbitrary code execution without authentication.

item.title: Schneider Electric patches Rapsody software use-after-free flaw
item.description: CISA has published an advisory for a use-after-free vulnerability in Schneider Electric EcoStruxure Power Build Rapsody software that allows local code execution via malicious files.

item.title: Microsoft warns of potential printing failures for Forcepoint users after hotpatch
item.description: The November 2026 Windows hotpatch may cause Print Spooler failures on Windows 11 24H2 systems running Forcepoint DLP Endpoint Agent.

item.title: Peruvian call centre operator jailed for $15m government impersonation fraud
item.description: A Lima-based operator was sentenced to eight years for managing call centres that defrauded over 30,000 Spanish-speaking US residents.

item.title: NYSDFS settles $6.75m with Rocket Mortgage and Mr. Cooper
item.description: New York regulators announced settlements with two major mortgage lenders, highlighting the importance of effective multi-factor authentication controls and timely incident reporting.

item.title: Cyberattack disrupts Guadeloupe university hospital IT systems
item.description: A major cyberattack on Saturday night forced the Guadeloupe university hospital to activate its emergency response plan and postpone non-emergency procedures.

item.title: GlobeTopper loses $2.5m after API credential theft
item.description: A cyberattack on B2B gift card distributor GlobeTopper resulted in $2.5m in lost revenue and the redemption of $70,000 in digital gift cards.

item.title: LaLiga confirms cyberattack exposed fan personal data
item.description: Spain's top football league disclosed that a cybercriminal accessed its fan services platform between 14 and 16 November, extracting personal data from registered users.

item.title: RansomwareHelp CTO indicted for wire fraud after FBI sting
item.description: The co-founder of a firm claiming to decrypt ransomware without payment has been charged with wire fraud after an FBI operation revealed he was secretly paying attackers and charging victims a markup.

item.title: CISA adds MONAI Label and Mail Assure flaws to KEV Catalog
item.description: CISA has added two critical vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog, citing active exploitation of a path traversal flaw in MONAI Label and an SSRF issue in N-able Mail Assure.

item.title: Verizon report: Credential abuse drives 13% of breaches
item.description: Verizon's 2026 Data Breach Investigations Report identifies credential abuse as the initial access vector in 13% of breaches.

item.title: Michigan nurse jailed for $1.6m Medicare fraud using stolen records
item.description: A home health care owner was sentenced to four years in prison for billing Medicare for services that were never performed, using stolen patient data.

item.title: Austrian Foreign Ministry website breached, diplomat contacts exposed
item.description: A breach of an external website exposed official contact details for Austrian diplomats, with no attribution yet made.

item.title: Human Security disrupts BadBox 3.0 ad fraud botnet
item.description: The third iteration of the BadBox operation generated 40 billion daily bid requests by spoofing CTV apps on low-cost Android devices.
